stem:
Meena is making a greeting card at home that lights up. She connects an LED to a cell using wires.
An LED only allows current to pass through it in one direction. It glows only when its longer terminal is connected to the positive side of the cell and its shorter terminal is connected to the negative side.
In which connection will the LED glow?

options.text: longer terminal to the negative side of the cell and shorter terminal to the positive side
longer terminal to the positive side of the cell and shorter terminal to the negative side
both terminals of the LED joined to the positive side of the cell
both terminals of the LED joined to the negative side of the cell

teacher.key_rationale: An LED conducts in one direction only and glows when its longer (positive) terminal is connected to the positive side of the cell and its shorter (negative) terminal to the negative side, which is option B. Option A reverses the polarity so no current flows; options C and D connect both terminals to the same side, so there is no potential difference across the LED and it stays off.
